findings: Exact archive/manifest pins bind fresh native deployment before the helper is uploaded; resource profile and native/probe/outer deadlines remain unchanged.
Manifest reader uses no-follow nonblocking descriptors, regular-file/size checks and bounded reads after arming its timer; FIFO/symlink/oversize controls cover the initial review finding.

Selected files are closed manifest rows under explicit runtime prefixes; descriptor-relative traversal rejects escapes, symlinks, nonregular files and multiple links. All rows are preflighted before advice.

Only fdatasync and POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED act on selected read-only file descriptors. No global cache controls, cgroup writes, body writes, source mutation, scheduler changes, provider calls or verifier execution are added.

Stable inode/device/mode/link/ownership/size/time metadata is checked before and after advice and on final reopen. Tests also compare actual bytes. Runtime model/source owners independently validate selected assets later.
Hint failures are counted separately and never reported as successful reclamation. Wrapper telemetry labels global_drop_caches=False without asserting that pages were or were not reclaimed.
limitations: Candidate deliberately avoids rereading selected bodies, so byte-hash validation relies on the fresh verified deployment and later native asset consumers; metadata checks do not replace cryptographic content validation.
POSIX advice is best effort. Available-memory change and admission/inference success must be measured in the authorized diagnostic, not inferred from these controls.
No test, Docker, model or provider execution was performed by this reviewer.
scope: Off-tree diagnostic only; no production code changes or benchmark/qualification claims by this review.
